quotations.quote: BACKGROUND: Effects of coffee on the gastrointestinal system have been suggested by patients and the lay press, while doctors tend to discourage its consumption in some diseases.
METHODS: The literature on the effects of coffee and caffeine on the gastrointestinal system is reviewed with emphasis on gastrointestinal function.
RESULTS: Although often mentioned as a cause of dyspeptic symptoms, no association between coffee and dyspepsia is found. Heartburn is the most frequently reported symptom after coffee drinking.

quotations.quote: SUBJECTS, MATERIALS AND METHODS: 10 young asymptomatic habitual coffee drinkers were included in the study.
The probands underwent SaLM test twice--first time without coffee restriction and second time after 48-hour coffee abstinence.
Permeability for sucrose was significantly higher in the group of habitual coffee drinkers in comparison with non-coffee drinkers (p < 0.01).
